title: Tokenized surface blend modes and curve gamma for accessible dark theme
creator: Evelyn Zhao
description: Background: As we expand compact, high-density surfaces (tables, dense forms, and compact buttons) we see contrast regressions in dark theme when using simple alpha-layering on top of a single neutral background. This ticket introduces a tokenized system for surface blending that makes two changes: 1) explicit blend-mode tokens (per-surface blending approach: sRGB alpha, linearized alpha, perceptual (L*), and overlay curves) and 2) a curve/gamma token that parameterizes how colors are blended (to preserve perceived contrast at small sizes). Goal: create a repeatable token surface model that designers and engineers can apply to components so dark-mode surfaces maintain accessibility at small text sizes and 1px dividers while keeping the visual hierarchy and motion-friendly elevation cues.
design_decisions: Introduce tokens for surface blend strategy: surface.blend.strategy.{default,linear,perceptual,overlay}
Add numeric token surface.blend.gamma that controls gamma curve used when compositing (default 2.2 for sRGB, perceptual uses 1.8-2.0 tuning)
Define surface steps as tokens: surface.step.{0..5} each stores a blended color, blend alpha, and elevation shadow preset reference
Prefer perceptual blending (CIE L*a*b* interpolation) for small, high-contrast UI elements to reduce perceived contrast collapse in dark themes
Keep token names semantic and composable to allow runtime mixing in client libraries (e.g., tokenized inputs: base-surface + blend-strategy + step-index)
Provide guidance for when to prefer linearized alpha for high-performance path vs perceptual for accuracy in server-side compiled themes
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens and examples created for surface.blend.strategy and surface.blend.gamma in both light and dark themes
A/B visual QA comparing old alpha-only surfaces to new blend-mode tokens across dense table and compact button states shows improved contrast for text at 12px and 14px in dark theme
Engineering has a spec and code examples for computing surface.step tokens at runtime (JS reference) and fallback token values for platforms without LAB libs
Docs and design kit include interactive Figma components showing surface step interpolation across gamma values
No regressions for existing light theme tokens and clear migration notes for component owners
tasks: Audit current dark theme surfaces and list components impacted (tables, compact buttons, dense cards, form fields)
Create token proposal JSON and PRD describing new tokens and runtime contract
Prototype perceptual blending for surface.step tokens in Figma (with plugin) and produce visual diff screenshots
Work with Eng: produce minimal JS utility (surface-blend.js) and sample CSS vars for fallback
Add migration plan and rollout schedule in the Console docs and release notes
comments: 2026-03-10 — Evelyn Zhao: Initial ticket created. Observed contrast failures on dense tables when using single alpha overlay; proposing tokenized approach that includes blend gamma.
2026-03-11 — Aisha Patel: Reviewed and added blending strategy options. Requesting small prototypes in Figma before locking gamma defaults.

2026-03-12 — Miguel Santos (Eng): Engineering note — we should provide both a simple CSS-variable fallback (sRGB alpha) and a JS runtime for perceptual blending. We'll estimate effort after seeing the PRD.

2026-03-13 — Accessibility review (June Park): Preliminary check — perceptual blending likely improves small text contrast in dark themes but we must validate with automated contrast checks and manual testing on OLED screens.
2026-03-14 — Aisha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria and added migration steps. Assigned prototype work to design.
notes: Implementation choices: where possible, encourage component libraries to compute surface.step tokens at build time for static bundles and at runtime for theme switches. Keep a small set of canonical gamma presets (0.9, 1.0, 1.8, 2.2) to reduce cognitive overhead. Add visual tests in Percy for compact tables/buttons.
